title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-12
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Behringer Ultramatch SRC2000 -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Flawless soundboard recording of a high‑energy 10/12/68 Avalon show highlighted by an epic Dark Star, The Eleven and The Other One
ai_review.review: The Miller‑upgraded soundboard capture is crystal‑clear and balanced, letting the band’s incendiary playing shine.  Fans rave about a blistering first set that rolls into a second set packed with a 15‑minute Dark Star, a jaw‑dropping Eleven, an otherworldly Other One/​Cryptical sequence and a fiery New Potato Caboose.  Jerry’s lead work and Phil’s bass solo are repeatedly praised, while the lack of Pigpen’s organ is noted but not seen as detracting from the tight, high‑octane performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 60 reviews, >90 % five‑star, consistently praising both musical and technical aspects; only a few minor criticisms (pigpen absence, one 0‑star outlier).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller “upgrade” yields a crisp, clean mix with virtually no hiss; occasional mention of slight pitch correction but overall flawless clarity and balance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set tight and energetic, second set maintains momentum with a few rough transitions (e.g., into New Potato) but overall flow is praised as seamless and powerful.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for blistering leads, perfect tone, soaring vocals and overall guitar brilliance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a “Thirteens‑jam” style solo during New Potato and strong bass presence throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for sweet vocal moments (e.g., New Potato) and solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is absent, which some reviewers miss; otherwise keyboards are considered adequate for the era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally solid; one reviewer mentions a slightly weak drum segment, but overall the percussion drives the high‑energy jams.
